claim: Standard frequentist significance tests cannot statistically support the null hypothesis of zero effect; a non-significant p-value only means the data are not surprising under the null, not that no effect exists. The TOST (two one-sided tests) procedure is the standard remedy: it specifies lower/upper equivalence bounds based on the smallest effect size of interest (SESOI) and rejects effects more extreme than those bounds.
stance_target: General methodological standard for equivalence testing applicable to any small-sample null-result reporting, including ML benchmark comparisons
scope_conditions: frequentist Neyman-Pearson hypothesis testing framework; originates in pharmacokinetics (Hauck & Anderson 1984), formalized as TOST by Schuirmann 1987
quoted_support: It is statistically impossible to support the hypothesis that a true effect size is exactly zero. What is possible in a frequentist hypothesis testing framework is to statistically reject effects large enough to be deemed worthwhile.

claim: Rejecting small effects in an equivalence test requires large samples; with narrow equivalence bounds, in most cases only a meta-analysis-scale sample will have sufficient statistical power.
stance_target: The audited paper's decision to report its Design-Bench null as 'no detectable difference, never equivalence' rather than running/foregrounding a positive TOST equivalence claim at n=7 tasks
scope_conditions: TOST equivalence tests for t-tests, correlations, and meta-analyses in psychology; general to any small-n paired/independent comparison
quoted_support: Rejecting small effects in an equivalence test requires large samples. If researchers want to perform an equivalence test with narrow equivalence bounds (e.g., ΔL = -.1 and ΔU = .1), in most cases, only a meta-analysis will have sufficient statistical power.

claim: The TOST procedure is explicitly formulated for dependent (paired) means as well as independent means, using Cohen's dz for the paired case -- directly matching a per-task paired comparison design (e.g. n=7 paired task-level score differences) rather than only independent-groups designs.
stance_target: Applicability of TOST methodology to a paired per-task ML benchmark comparison design
quoted_support: Equivalence Tests for Differences Between Dependent Means. When comparing dependent means, the correlation between the observations has to be taken into account, and the effect size directly related to the statistical significance of the test... is Cohen's dz.

claim: In small samples where confidence intervals are wide, a study may have essentially no statistical power for an equivalence test at all, because the CI will necessarily be wider than the equivalence bounds -- meaning an inconclusive/undetermined TOST result (neither significantly different from zero nor significantly equivalent) is the expected, uninformative outcome at small n.
stance_target: The claim that a TOST run at n=7 tasks would be predictably uninformative and thus carries limited additional evidential weight beyond the existing non-significance framing
scope_conditions: general TOST power analysis under small samples
quoted_support: It is important to take statistical power into account when determining the equivalence bounds because, in small samples (where CIs are wide), a study might have no statistical power (i.e., the CI will always be so wide that it is necessarily wider than the equivalence bounds).

claim: No paper specific to equivalence/non-inferiority testing for ML benchmark comparisons at small n was found via OpenAlex/arXiv searches ('equivalence test machine learning benchmark', 'TOST equivalence testing algorithm comparison', 'non-inferiority testing machine learning model comparison'); results were dominated by unrelated ML application papers or medical/clinical equivalence-testing papers, confirming Wave 1's negative result. Lakens (2017) is the field-general (psychology-originated but domain-agnostic) methodological reference that best supports the audited paper's small-n TOST framing.
stance_target: Existence of ML-benchmarking-specific equivalence-testing guidance (Target 3 of this research task)
scope_conditions: OpenAlex and arXiv API searches conducted 2026-07-20
quoted_support: N/A -- absence finding from academic-API search, not a quotable passage from this source.
